# Application shortcuts and automatic delivery

6 October 2026: the [assembled Chromium comparison](../../../../docs/verification/browser-direct-transport/README.md#chromium-through-the-application) reuses all fifteen recording/Command/Live workflows and 102 complete states in this owner. Its 4,175-byte differential fixture is independently reconstructed against the unchanged Firefox and GTK fixtures before native execution. Actual provider bodies, clipboard, DOM, stores, public controls and normal shutdown match the reference; the native app activates Chromium without manual accessibility controls. Chromium's incorrect Unicode range remains visible in insertion and Command input. A separate nonempty ASCII read control rejects an actual empty `(0,0)` read. Both browser variants and the original eight GTK workflows/34 states plus the held-readiness fault pass; the strict whole-workflow statuses remain Pending.

6 October 2026: the [assembled Firefox Live comparison](../../../../docs/verification/browser-direct-transport/README.md#live-through-the-application) adds six independently observed workflows/47 states to this same owner. Global committed dictation inserts once; manual/changed-focus delivery stays copy-only; final drafts save and copy without a second paste. Actual endpoint holds expose revision guards, premature review Copy refusal, paused draft saving and cancellation with a late result. All previous recording/Command and original GTK observations are preserved; the browser target now runs fifteen workflows/102 states with real outgoing read controls and normal cleanup.

6 October 2026: the [assembled Firefox Command comparison](../../../../docs/verification/browser-direct-transport/README.md#command-through-the-application) adds five independently observed workflows/36 states to the same owner. Apply replaces the exact selection or inserts at its caret once; Discard preserves clipboard and target; another focused field forces copying; manual recording stays copy-only. Full public preview controls, raw/output/History, clipboard, DOM/events, portal closure and original speech/rewrite requests match. The native target now runs nine browser workflows/55 states. All earlier recording observations and original GTK fixtures are preserved.

6 October 2026: the [Firefox application comparison](../../../../docs/verification/browser-direct-transport/README.md#recording-through-the-application) reuses this existing owner, inputs and common states for four additional browser workflows. All 19 independently observed source/native states match, including exact Unicode target data, one-attempt insertion, copy-only recovery and both portal callers' shutdown. The new browser fixture shares repeated observations and retains actual outgoing read controls. `make linux-browser-application-test` selects that variant with normal caches and transport defaults; these original GTK observations remain unchanged.

The immutable reference is Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. [The independent fixture](released-application-shortcuts.json), SHA-256 `1f556ecf98a75575c353b76b86daec9dc7efe5bd7c97083dddbc3c93f280fef5`, contains eight actual application workflows and 34 GTK, preference, History, clipboard and separate-target states. The external observer activates the unchanged released application, invokes registered actions and real widgets, and receives real portal signals. Every imported released module is checked against the pinned commit; no handler is replaced. The observer stays in ignored `tmp/`; native verification invokes no interpreter.

The native check constructs the real `ApplicationDesktop` and its services. Both applications use the separate native portal, PCM and GTK text-target processes, plus a loopback speech endpoint. Actual binding requests, replacement/closure traces, caller disconnects, uploaded audio, provider responses and saved delivery outcomes are compared. The target independently reports text, caret/selection, focus, edit count and editability. Generated process/request identities use the existing peer's ownership checks and per-session numbering; the captured text and provider payloads remain exact. Capture labels use the existing capture observer's documented private-path/timing normalization. The fixture pins GTK 4.22.4 and Pango 1.58.2.

The bootstrap regression exposed intermittent `GetItems` warnings while the original test repeatedly created/destroyed GTK roots and text targets inside one client process. A separate observer mapped the failing accessibility names to those private processes. The maintained test now starts a fresh client for every workflow and the readiness fault. It presents a small real GTK harness window before initializing libatspi and retains that process's accessibility cache through the tested owner's shutdown; production target tracking excludes that window by its ordinary own-process rule. The default accessibility cache remains enabled. Each child keeps the same frozen assertions and the parent rejects warning/critical diagnostics. The final eight-workflow/34-state run and readiness fault pass without warnings in `tmp/bootstrap-shortcut-processes/`; earlier warning-bearing attempts are not accepted evidence. Child output uses files because the ordinary clipboard owner can retain an inherited descriptor after its test client exits.

Global recording replaces the selected `🐎` in `Before 🐎 after` exactly once with `Portal dictation keeps 12 files.`. A repeated activation while the key is held does not stop capture. Changing the recording key during capture is rejected and restores the saved choice. Starting with the on-screen action remains copy-only even when a global key stops it; cancellation preserves the target and clipboard. Rejected portal approval still leaves the copy-only button usable. Latest-conversation activation navigates from History and reopens a hidden window.

The actual preferences replace F9 with F11, preserve the requesting/approved labels, ignore activation from the old session, display compositor-assigned F12 and CTRL+R, and update the automatic-paste hint. Ordinary provider changes retain the current portal session. Initial missing credentials prevent portal creation; repairing the provider enables recording, while explicit setup acknowledgement starts shortcut registration and clears the retained startup callout. Exit during approval closes its outstanding request/session and waits for the private caller to disconnect. Capture exits additionally require audio-child reaping and recording-file cleanup.

Before application wiring, the first comparison failed waiting for portal registration. A further native fault changes the real recording-key dropdown while a separate synthetic keyring process is still resolving startup credentials. Before repair, capture became ready with saved F11 but the portal trace stayed empty: the newer settings task had discarded startup's registration responsibility. The root now carries startup/Retry through the latest readiness generation, registers only the current key once, and rejects the stale result. The fault also requires a ready status, acknowledged portal shutdown, no retained keyring process and no History entry. This additional asynchronous fault is distinct from the eight released workflows; the released synchronous startup cannot expose that intermediate UI state. No speech upload occurs in this fault.

Build the native development peers, then execute the ignored check in the guarded private runner:

```sh
cargo build --locked -p mluva-audio --bin audio-fixture-peer --bin mluva-audio-cleanup
cargo build --locked -p mluva-providers --bin credential-fixture-peer
cargo build --locked -p mluva-gtk --example text_target_peer
bash dev/run-isolated-browser.sh tmp/application-shortcut-evidence -- bash -c '
  export PATH="$OFFSCREEN_SESSION_ROOT/application-shortcut-tools:$PATH"
  TZ=UTC cargo test --locked -p mluva-gtk --test application_shortcuts -- --ignored --nocapture
'
```

The portal peer is now a Cargo fixture binary and is built/located automatically by the test. `MLUVA_DISABLE_GLOBAL_SHORTCUT` must be absent for this check. The separate [assembled-application comparison](application-evidence.md) requires it to be set, matching its released observer. The runner provides private HOME/XDG, DISPLAY, accessibility/session buses, network/PID namespaces and masked devices; both test and peers guard that boundary. No host clipboard, input, portal, microphone, credentials or user content is used. Development peers are excluded from distribution.

This proves application ownership and real target delivery through a controlled portal. It does not prove physical function keys, compositor approval UI, every target/toolkit, single-instance/background bootstrap, the actual Omarchy widget, screenshots/narration, physical recording, packaging, Python removal or performance. Test applications use registered `NON_UNIQUE` identities and explicit main-context iteration; hide/reopen is not a complete resident-executable acceptance check. All complete-workflow rows remain Pending and the installed app/widget remain 1.6.0.
